summary: We developed "Sound Signal — The Earth Information Jukebox Accessible", a web application contained in a single HTML5 file that transforms NASA satellite images and visualizations into polyphonic symphonies and automatic Colombian Sign Language (LSC) modules. Our project addresses the accessibility challenge by translating climate and planetary data into a real-time multisensory experience; to achieve this, our software scans the image's pixels and maps their color values (hue, lightness, and saturation) to a 14-tone harmonic musical scale based on Newton's theory. This solution is important because it closes a historical gap of scientific exclusion: we make it possible for visually impaired people and the deaf community to interact with complex geospatial information (such as ocean currents, CO₂ emissions, or air quality) autonomously, equitably, and through an open-source format.
details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works: Our system executes a continuous, low-latency spatial scan over satellite maps and converts colors into motion, harmony, and articulation. We employ a cluster of four independent cursors that act as polyphonic voices (Soprano, Alto, Tenor, Bass) to interpret the North, South, and Equator of the image. Simultaneously, we programmed an algorithm that associates dominant colors with textual descriptors compatible with screen readers and triggers synchronized video clips in LSC.

Benefits and expected impact: We offer the benefit of autonomy in spatial data exploration, replacing visual barriers with acoustic and gestural feedback. Our expected impact is to bring Earth observation to inclusive schools, environmental monitoring centers, and "NASA Earth Information Center" kiosks, allowing planetary science to reach millions of people without relying on sight.

Tools, languages, and software: We developed the platform entirely using standard web technologies: HTML5, CSS (via TailwindCSS), and JavaScript. We built the spatial acoustic engine using the Tone.js library for 3D synthesizer and sampler management. Additionally, we integrated local artificial intelligence through the ViT-GPT2 neural network (Hugging Face) to generate automatic descriptions directly in the browser without relying on paid APIs.

Project creativity: The most creative aspect of our solution lies in unifying formal musicology with remote sensing. Instead of emitting simple radar tones, we composed structured musical arrangements, using voice leading logic at a distance of fewer than 5 semitones and harmonic arpeggios conditioned purely by the patterns of the Earth's geography.

Factors considered by the team: As a team, we carefully considered both technical and physical accessibility. We ensured that the program was a lightweight, single-file web tool capable of working online, we optimized the latency to 60 FPS to prevent auditory delays during users' tactile interaction, and we included a high-contrast mode for people with partial vision.
